text:
Sampling semantics differ across implementations. The [official PyTorch gSASRec sampler](https://github.com/asash/gSASRec-pytorch/blob/main/dataset_utils.py) draws uniform negatives with replacement, without excluding training histories or current targets; duplicates remain, and target collisions receive contradictory positive/negative labels. Repeated targets remain separate sequence-position examples. By comparison, [TensorFlow sampled softmax](https://www.tensorflow.org/api_docs/python/tf/nn/sampled_softmax_loss) removes sampled-target collisions by default, but does not automatically exclude other user positives. Its [candidate sampler](https://www.tensorflow.org/api_docs/python/tf/random/uniform_candidate_sampler) explicitly distinguishes replacement from unique sampling and supplies corresponding expected counts.

Uncorrected sampled cross-entropy optimizes classification within the sampled candidate multiset. Duplicate negatives contribute repeatedly to its denominator; deduplicating changes the objective. Corrected sampled softmax subtracts log expected sampling counts, rather than an arbitrary popularity adjustment. With identical uniform expected counts for every candidate, corrections cancel; this does not apply automatically when the positive is inserted deterministically and negatives come from a target-excluding distribution. Inference: rejecting all training positives creates a user-dependent proposal, q_u(i)=1/(|I|−|H_u|) on unseen items and zero elsewhere. A full-catalog correction cannot simply apply log q_u to the excluded target; explicitly define the positive contribution, supported denominator and replacement/inclusion probabilities. Repeated targets used as shared or in-batch candidates require collision masking for every matching ID.

[gBCE](https://github.com/asash/gSASRec-pytorch) instead weights the positive log-sigmoid term by β=1−t+tα, with α=k/(|I|−1), while retaining binary negative terms. Its calibration claims depend on sampling assumptions; history exclusion changes those assumptions. Sampled cross-entropy is a reasonable reproducible ranking alternative, provided sampling, masking, multiplicity, correction and reduction are specified. It is neither BCE-equivalent nor automatically calibrated like gBCE.
